observations: body L1, L3: the first e of «aequatoris» (L1) prints broken, as a small raised stroke; a speck stands to the right of «horizontis (1).» (L3).
body L1, L4, L11, L13: «al–Battānī» is letter-spaced in L1 and L4, not in L11; «al–Bīrūnī» (L13) is letter-spaced. The long dashes measure 5.4 pt in L1, L4 and L11 and 5.3 pt in L13.

body L4-L7: the translation, p. 118, l. 14-28, gives the quantities of appearance in degrees of the signs for one clima only, the fourth («quartum clima delegimus», l. 18), that of the latitude 36° of ar-Raqqah. The dashes of «14–28», «142–43» and «ar–Raqqah» measure 5.3, 5.3 and 5.3 pt; «Ptolemaei» (L6) is letter-spaced.
body L8-L10: «Ḥabash», «Oloug Beg» and «Barhebraeus» are letter-spaced. The dashes of «67,v.–70,v.», «73,r.–76,v.» and «79–80» measure 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5 pt, the dash before «Barhebraeus» 9.6 pt.

body L11-L13: «Indi» is letter-spaced; specks stand before «ut» and under the e of «statuerunt» (L11). The dashes of «Sūrya–Siddhānta», «Burgess–Whitney», «4–9», «246–47» and «90–92» measure 5.3 to 5.4 pt; the dash of «365–» (L12) is joined to the 5 and that of «–67» (L13) to the 6, each about 5.4 pt beyond the figure.
body L14-L16: the head of the chapter is set in the larger type, as printed. The dash after «a)» measures 10.3 pt; that of «3–41» is joined to the 3 and the 4, about 6.3 pt between them.
body L18: «al–‘ulūm» has a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L23-L37: the Greek follows Ptolemy and Halma's French as printed: «subsolaire», «simultané» (the accent faint in L28), «sub-/sequent» without an accent and divided with a hyphen of 4.1 pt, «c. m.» for «coucher matutinal». The α of this Greek type is shaped like an x in several words (ἐπανατολή, μεσουράνημα, σχηματισμοί, ἑῷα); the final ις of «ἐπικατάδυσις» (L32) prints broken, like «υσ:ς»; a speck stands over «πρόδυσις» (L33). The dashes of «100–» and «–104» (L24-L25) measure 6.0 and 5.5 pt.

body L23: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXV; AB01-PDF0442-body-L009 to L018) add that these configurations of the stars with the Sun, of no use to us, served astrology: Ptolemy himself, Tetrabiblos II, 7, on the forecasts drawn from eclipses, bids take of the fixed stars the one most familiar to the place of the eclipse, first by its brightness in the preceding angle, according to the configurations apparent in nine modes that he set out in his first Syntaxis, the Almagest, and then in the angle of the ascendant or of the midheaven that follows the place of the eclipse.

notes_left L1-L4: the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 7.8 pt. «Abû» (L4) is letter-spaced, and its circumflex, like the circumflexes of the names that follow it in the right column, prints as a single slanting stroke, as on p. 248 (notes); the circumflex of «Mafâtih» prints as a circumflex; the hyphen of «al-‘olûm» measures 3.5 pt.

notes_right L1-L4: «‘Abdallâh Mohammed al-Khowârezmî» is letter-spaced; the d of «edidit» prints broken. The hyphen of «229-230» measures 3.7 pt and the dash before «Liber» 8.2 pt. The years 363 and 381 of the Hiǵrah began on 2 October 973 and 20 March 991 (Julian, by the tabular calendar).
